My SO and I both work full time jobs M-F. However, my commute to work is much worse than his, I typically drive for ~25-30 min in the morning and 40-45 min in the afternoon (rush hour). He leaves work to go home at 4pm, an hour earlier before I do, he avoids traffic and only has a 10-15 min commute to work each way. My afternoons feel very flustered, rush hour traffic is extremely difficult to navigate where I live - tractor trailers will tailgate you, people swerve back and forth without any regard safety, many are going too fast or too slow, there are always accidents, and whenever I glance over to the other lanes I see someone texting about 50% of the time. It's dangerous and I've been lucky to only have been in one fender bender since driving on the interstate in the past 4 years (their fault, he was texting and driving and hit me from behind). By the time I've gotten home he's already had an hour and half to decompress and relax from his day. When I get home he's ready to go to the grocery store or go out to dinner, and because my car is always behind his I end up driving to wherever we need to go. We have this unwritten rule that whoever is in the back of the driveway (always me) drives us. The times we do swap places it's just annoying and time consuming.

I know these are small annoyances in the grand scheme of things, it's just frustrating for me because I feel like I never have time to decompress after work/traffic. When I voice my complaints about this to him he seems to think I'm just complaining for the sake of complaining. I've tried talking to him about prepping our meals a week ahead of time so we only have to hit up the grocery store once or twice a week, but he says he can't plan that far ahead for food because he doesn't know if he'll be in the mood for X, Y or Z food that day.

I'm stressed because I don't have any time to decompress after a long day before I'm on the move again, and I end up driving the two of us most of the time. I don't think I'm doing a great job at explaining my reasoning why I'm stressed in the afternoons.
